title: Diabetes and Cataracts Development-Characteristics, Subtypes and Predictive Modeling Using Machine Learning in Romanian Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
summary: A cross-sectional study of 201 cataract patients, 105 of them with diabetes, applied random-forest classification to cataract subtype combinations. Cortical cataract was significantly more frequent in diabetes (p<0.0001), and diabetes status, duration and diabetic polyneuropathy were important classification features. This is an exploratory cohort-specific association and classification result, not longitudinal prediction of cataract development. The study does not establish external generalization, causal effects or sustained operational impact.
ai_technology: Random Forest classification predicts one-, two- or three-subtype cataract associations from patient factors; model is applied to a cross-sectional cohort.
organization: Doctoral School of Medicine, "Victor Babes" University of Medicine and Pharmacy, 300041 Timisoara, Romania

evidence.tested: cortical cataract was significantly more frequent among patients with diabetes (p<0.0001); nuclear and posterior subcapsular differences were not statistically significant. Diabetes presence/duration and polyneuropathy ranked as important classifier inputs.
evidence.unknown: Methods/Results: 201-patient cross-sectional dataset, 105 diabetic participants, with a train/test split; no external or prospective validation, so title language about development should not be read as longitudinal prediction.
evidence.ai_role: Random Forest classification predicts one-, two- or three-subtype cataract associations from patient factors; model is applied to a cross-sectional cohort.
